subject: NexaHealth DPA redline — analytics export & subprocessor clarification
body:
From: Contracts, NexaHealth <contracts@nexahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NexaHealth - Proposed DPA (redline v3)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — attached is our proposed DPA with a couple of requested redlines. Two items I want to call out up-front: 1) an analytics export clause that would allow us to receive aggregated runtime telemetry for compliance reporting, and 2) an explicit subprocessor allowlist that includes two vendors (DataOpsCloud and TelemetryHub).

Files attached: NXH_DPA_redline_v3.pdf, subprocessors_list.xlsx

Can your legal/product/security review and confirm whether these are acceptable or if you need counter language? We are hoping to get sign-off before our pilot kickoff (target 9/15).

Thanks,
Amelia Harrow
Contracts, NexaHealth

---

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts, NexaHealth <contracts@nexahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: NexaHealth - Proposed DPA (redline v3)

Looping in Legal/Product/Security for quick triage. Key asks from the customer: analytics export (aggregated runtime telemetry) + specific subprocessor allowlist.

Quick context: NexaHealth needs aggregated telemetry for their audit. They call out DataOpsCloud and TelemetryHub as subprocessors that would handle export/analytics. Legal attached redline + subproc list. See RED-981 for internal notes.

Can Product weigh in on feasibility/effort and whether a limited export schema is possible? Security — can you evaluate the subprocessor list and suggest conditional language (SOC2, data minimization, no raw PII, etc.) if we want to accept? Olga — legal will likely want a targeted counterproposal. We need a consolidated ask back to the customer by 9/08 to keep pilot timeline.

Thanks — Tessa
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

---

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts, NexaHealth <contracts@nexahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NexaHealth - Proposed DPA (redline v3)

Thanks Tessa. I reviewed their PDF — two immediate negotiation points:

- Analytics export: Their draft would permit delivery of "operational telemetry" to NexaHealth. We should narrow this to a specific schema and frequency (e.g., daily aggregated metrics, top-line usage counts, no model inputs/outputs, explicit prohibition on re-identification).
- Subprocessor allowlist: They expect explicit approval for DataOpsCloud and TelemetryHub. We can accept a conditional allowlist if they commit to vendor attestations (SOC 2 Type II) and limit access to aggregates.

Proposed counter language (high level) I recommend we send: allow exports of aggregated operational metrics only; require customer to accept the export schema; require SOC2 attestation for listed subprocessors and a breach notification SLA tied to our own.

Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NexaHealth - Proposed DPA (redline v3)

Thanks Olga — flagged a couple product implications. Short summary:

- Export schema: We can produce daily aggregated metrics (counts, 95th latency percentiles, token volume buckets) that do not include prompts/responses or any identifiers. That would be ~2 weeks of work to define schema + build the export pipeline and another 1 week to QA and document.
- Runtime routing/subproc: If DataOpsCloud or TelemetryHub need access to runtime logs for their ingestion, we must ensure KV cache and user-level metadata are redacted. That adds ~1 sprint of work if we need to implement automated redaction rules and an export gating feature.
- Impact to roadmap: This is not a blocker for the pilot but will require a small focused spike (approx 3 dev-weeks). We need Product PM approval and Security sign-off on allowed fields.

Questions for Security: can we allow a technical pattern where the export pipeline produces a strictly schema-validated file and the subprocessor only receives that file (no runtime API access)? If yes, what attestations do we need from the vendor?

Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Inference

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NexaHealth - Proposed DPA (redline v3)

Appreciate the details. Security assessment (high-level):

- DataOpsCloud: unknown maturity in our vendor inventory. They need SOC 2 Type II and a data processing statement that limits use to the specified export files. No long-term storage beyond 90 days unless mutually agreed and logged.
- TelemetryHub: listed as having SOC 2 Type II but we need the last attestation report and a questionnaire about access controls (who can download exports).
- Technical approach: the safest pattern is the one Karthik suggested — a schema-validated export file pushed to a restricted S3 bucket we control; grant the subprocessor a short-lived role scoped to read only that bucket and only the relevant prefix. That avoids giving runtime API access.

Counterproposal language I recommend: "Redwood may provide aggregated operational metrics as a schema-defined export. Exported artifacts will not include model inputs/outputs or customer-identifying information. Subprocessors named in the agreement must provide SOC2 Type II attestation and accept a limited-purpose data processing attachment; any subprocessor access will be scoped via short-lived credentials to a designated export artifact store."

Attached is a short security evaluation note with requirements and a proposed checklist (security_evaluation_note.txt).

Marcus
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

---

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts, NexaHealth <contracts@nexahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Sep 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidated position for customer — action items and timeline

Thanks team — this is helpful. Next steps I propose:

1) Olga: prepare a short counterproposal email to NexaHealth that includes the counter language Marcus suggested and explicitly states the export is limited to the agreed schema (please reference RED-981 and attach NXH_DPA_redline_v3.pdf).
2) Karthik: confirm schema fields (we should enumerate the daily fields and provide an ETA for the 3-week delivery). If you can get a prototype spec by Fri 09/08 that would be ideal.
3) Marcus: finalize the security checklist and confirm vendor attestations required. If DataOpsCloud lacks SOC2, propose an interim mitigation (short-lived credentials + no raw logs).

Goal: sign-off back to NexaHealth by 2028-09-08 to keep pilot kickoff on 9/15. If anyone needs more time, flag now and we'll ask NexaHealth for a brief extension.

Tessa
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
